api/Axiam.Sdk.Options.AxiamClientOptions.summary: Class AxiamClientOptions Namespace Axiam.Sdk.Options Assembly Axiam.Sdk.dll Typed, options-pattern configuration for AxiamClient (Claude's Discretion, 21-RESEARCH.md/21-CONTEXT.md D-07). BaseUrl and TenantId are required here for the future AddAxiam()/ IOptions<AxiamClientOptions> DI registration path (plan 21-06) — AxiamClient's own tenant-required constructor (this plan, SC#1) sources the tenant/base-URL from its own explicit positional parameters instead, so SC#1's compile-time guarantee never depends on whether an options object happens to be supplied at all. public sealed record AxiamClientOptions : IEquatable<AxiamClientOptions> Inheritance object AxiamClientOptions Implements IEquatable<AxiamClientOptions> Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Properties BaseUrl Reserved for the future DI/options-pattern registration path (D-07, plan 21-06); AxiamClient's own constructor (this plan) always uses its own baseUrl parameter as the source of truth, never this field. public required Uri BaseUrl { get; init; } Property Value Uri ClientCertificatePem PEM-encoded client-certificate chain presented for mutual-TLS (mTLS) client authentication (CONTRACT.md §6.1): AXIAM binds this X.509 identity — signed by the tenant's organization CA — to a service account or IoT device. Applies to both the REST and gRPC transports of the same AxiamClient. Opt-in: null (the default) leaves the SDK's bearer-cookie behavior unchanged and presents no client certificate. MUST be set together with ClientKeyPem — supplying exactly one of the two is rejected with an ArgumentException at client construction. Presenting a client certificate NEVER relaxes strict server verification (§6.1 rule 2); this is a separate code path from CustomCaPem's server-trust callback. public byte[]? ClientCertificatePem { get; init; } Property Value byte[] ClientKeyPem PEM-encoded private key (PKCS#8 or PKCS#1) matching ClientCertificatePem, used for mutual-TLS client authentication (CONTRACT.md §6.1). Secret material (§7): it is never logged, serialized, or exposed via a public getter beyond this options record it is set on (mirrors CustomCaPem). MUST be set together with ClientCertificatePem; supplying exactly one of the two is rejected with an ArgumentException at client construction. public byte[]? ClientKeyPem { get; init; } Property Value byte[] ConnectTimeout TCP connect timeout for the SDK-owned HttpClient. public TimeSpan ConnectTimeout { get; init; } Property Value TimeSpan CustomCaPem PEM-encoded custom CA certificate bytes — the ONLY TLS escape hatch (CONTRACT.md §6/SC#4): an ADDITIVE chain-trust-store entry alongside the system trust store, never a bypass. null (the default) uses the system trust store only. public byte[]? CustomCaPem { get; init; } Property Value byte[] DecisionMemoTtl Enables the CONTRACT.md §17 client-side decision memo. Default: Zero, which means disabled — not "cache for zero time". public TimeSpan DecisionMemoTtl { get; init; } Property Value TimeSpan Remarks What you are accepting. The staleness bound is this TTL, in both directions. A grant revoked on the server can still read as allowed for up to the TTL, and a grant just added can still read as denied for up to the TTL. Reads-your-own-writes is not guaranteed. An admin UI that grants a role and immediately re-checks is the case that breaks, and it breaks silently. If that is your workload, leave this off. Clamped to 5 seconds rather than rejected. Allows and denies are memoized identically (asymmetric caching leaks the outcome through latency), failures are never memoized, and the memo is cleared on any credential change. ExpectedAudience The aud value local token verification requires (CONTRACT.md §10.1 rule 6). CONDITIONAL and unset by default: null means no audience check is performed at all; once set, a token whose aud does not contain it — including a token with no aud at all — is rejected. An application guarding a user-facing resource server should generally expect axiam:user; it is not defaulted, because a service-to-service guard legitimately expects a different audience. public string? ExpectedAudience { get; init; } Property Value string ExpectedIssuer The iss claim value local token verification requires (CONTRACT.md §10.1 rule 5). CONDITIONAL and unset by default: null means no issuer check is performed at all; once set, a token whose iss differs — or which carries no iss — is rejected. There is no default value and no hardcoded AXIAM issuer anywhere in this SDK; supply your deployment's own issuer. public string? ExpectedIssuer { get; init; } Property Value string JwksCacheTtl How long a fetched JWKS document is trusted before JwksVerifier forces a refetch. public TimeSpan JwksCacheTtl { get; init; } Property Value TimeSpan MaxRetryAttempts Attempt cap for the CONTRACT.md §16 bounded read-only retry policy. Defaults to 3 (1 initial + 2 retries). public int MaxRetryAttempts { get; init; } Property Value int Remarks This is now wired. Until D5 this property — and the two below — were a "reserved config surface ... not yet wired into any call path", so the SDK performed no read-only retries at all while presenting three knobs that looked like it did. Values above the contract's are clamped down, not honored. §16.1 permits an SDK to lower the attempt cap or disable retry outright, never to raise it: a caller who could raise it turns one client into the thundering herd this policy exists to prevent, and the whole point of §16 is eleven SDKs agreeing on one table. Setting 10 gets you 3; setting 1 gets you 1. Use RetryEnabled to turn retrying off. OidcClientId The relying party's OAuth2 client_id (CONTRACT.md §12.1), used on every §12 grant and matched against the ID token's aud/azp (§12.4 rule 4). Required before calling any §12 operation other than OidcDiscoverAsync — client_id comes from client configuration, not a per-call argument (§12 T1 reference judgment call 21). public string? OidcClientId { get; init; } Property Value string OidcClientSecret A confidential client's client_secret (CONTRACT.md §12.1). Omit for a public client: LoginClientCredentialsAsync, IntrospectAsync, and RevokeAsync then throw AuthError, client-side with no wire call (§12.1 note 4 — a public client cannot call them). Held behind Sensitive<T> internally once the client is constructed. public string? OidcClientSecret { get; init; } Property Value string OidcClockSkewSeconds The permitted ID-token clock skew, in seconds, for the exp/iat/ nbf checks (CONTRACT.md §12.4 rule 5). Clamped to [1, 60] — the contract forbids configuring it above 60 seconds; a non-positive or larger value falls back to the 60-second default rather than being honored. public int OidcClockSkewSeconds { get; init; } Property Value int OidcDiscoveryTtl The OIDC discovery-document cache TTL. Floored at 5 minutes per CONTRACT.md §12.3 rule 6 — a smaller configured value is silently raised to the floor. The default (5 minutes) already satisfies the floor. public TimeSpan OidcDiscoveryTtl { get; init; } Property Value TimeSpan OrgId Organization UUID resolved by the real AXIAM login/refresh endpoints (beyond CONTRACT.md §5's documented tenant-only minimum). Mutually exclusive with OrgSlug — set at most one. public Guid? OrgId { get; init; } Property Value Guid? OrgSlug Organization slug. Mutually exclusive with OrgId — set at most one. public string? OrgSlug { get; init; } Property Value string RequestTimeout Overall per-request timeout for the SDK-owned HttpClient. public TimeSpan RequestTimeout { get; init; } Property Value TimeSpan RetryBaseDelay Base delay for the §16 backoff. Defaults to 200ms; a larger value is clamped down to it, for the reason given on MaxRetryAttempts. public TimeSpan RetryBaseDelay { get; init; } Property Value TimeSpan RetryEnabled Enables the CONTRACT.md §16 bounded read-only retry policy. Default: true. public bool RetryEnabled { get; init; } Property Value bool Remarks Set false to make every operation exactly one attempt. That is the right choice for a caller who owns their own retry layer — they know their deadline and this SDK does not — but it is not a way to make failures quieter: a transient NetworkError simply surfaces immediately. RetryMaxDelay Ceiling on any single §16 backoff. Defaults to 5s; a larger value is clamped down to it, for the reason given on MaxRetryAttempts. public TimeSpan RetryMaxDelay { get; init; } Property Value TimeSpan TelemetryHook Installs a CONTRACT.md §19 telemetry sink. public TelemetryHook? TelemetryHook { get; init; } Property Value TelemetryHook Remarks It receives request start/end, §16 retry and §9 refresh events, so metrics can be wired without this package depending on any metrics library. A hook that throws cannot fail the operation that fired it (§19.2 rule 2), and no event payload can carry a token — the event hierarchy is closed with fixed property lists (§19.2 rule 3). It is invoked on the calling task, so it must not block. api/Axiam.Sdk.Reactor.ReactorConnections.title: Class ReactorConnections | AXIAM .NET SDK
api/Axiam.Sdk.Reactor.ReactorConnections.summary: Class ReactorConnections Namespace Axiam.Sdk.Reactor Assembly Axiam.Sdk.dll Broker connections for a reactor, with CONTRACT.md §8b enforced rather than described. public static class ReactorConnections Inheritance object ReactorConnections Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Why this class exists. Channel takes an already-open channel, and the caller owns its lifecycle. That is a reasonable division — but until now the §8b requirement travelling with it was a sentence of XML doc: "its connection MUST have been opened over amqps:// with a trusted CA". A doc-comment MUST is a note to whoever reads the doc comment. Someone who builds a RabbitMQ.Client.ConnectionFactory from an amqp:// URI and hands over the channel gets a working reactor, no warning, and signed-but-readable token decisions on the wire. This class is the enforcing alternative. Build the factory here and §8b holds by construction: the URI is checked, TLS is on with verification at its strict default, and there is no argument anywhere that turns either off. The Kotlin and Java SDKs ship the same helper against their own client library, deliberately — SDKs should not disagree about what a reactor is allowed to connect to. ReactorServeOptions still accepts any channel: enforcing at construction cannot retroactively constrain a channel someone else opened, and refusing to serve on one whose provenance cannot be inspected would break every legitimate custom setup to catch a mistake this class already prevents. The layering, once. HMAC signing (§8/§22.2) gives authenticity and replay protection across broker hops, which TLS cannot, because TLS terminates at the broker and the broker re-sends. TLS gives confidentiality, which HMAC cannot. A reactor's reply is an instruction to allow, deny or rewrite a token: it needs both, and neither substitutes for the other. ConnectionFactory factory = ReactorConnections.CreateConnectionFactory( "amqps://reactor:secret@broker.internal:5671/%2f", new X509Certificate2("/etc/axiam/broker-ca.pem")); await using IConnection connection = await factory.CreateConnectionAsync(); await using IChannel channel = await connection.CreateChannelAsync(); Methods CreateConnectionFactory(string, X509Certificate2?, X509Certificate2?) Builds a RabbitMQ.Client.ConnectionFactory for amqpUri, refusing anything but amqps://. public static ConnectionFactory CreateConnectionFactory(string amqpUri, X509Certificate2? brokerCaCertificate = null, X509Certificate2? clientCertificate = null) Parameters amqpUri string The broker URI. MUST be amqps:// (§8b rules 1 and 5); every other scheme is refused here rather than downgraded, because a fallback that works is a fallback that gets used. brokerCaCertificate X509Certificate2 The CA that issued a privately-issued broker certificate (§8b rule 2 — the common in-cluster case), or null to verify against the OS trust store only. Supplied as an additional trust anchor via RabbitMQ.Client.SslOption.CertificateValidationCallback; see the remarks on BuildValidationCallback(X509Certificate2) for why a callback is the mechanism and what it is careful not to become. clientCertificate X509Certificate2 A client certificate with its private key, for mutual TLS toward the broker (§8b rule 3), or null. A certificate without a usable private key is refused: half a client identity cannot authenticate, and connecting anyway would silently drop the mutual half of mutual TLS. Returns ConnectionFactory A factory whose connections verify the broker. Exceptions ArgumentException The URI is not amqps://, is unparseable, or the client certificate carries no private key. RequireAmqps(string) Rejects any URI that is not amqps:// (§8b rules 1 and 5). public static void RequireAmqps(string amqpUri) Parameters amqpUri string The broker URI to check. Remarks An unparseable URI is an error here, not a pass-through. A security check must fail closed on an input it cannot read — the opposite arrangement (skip the check when parsing fails) is a real bug that shipped in a sibling SDK. There is no loopback exception. §8b rules 1 and 5 carry no host carve-out, and the AXIAM server is TLS-only with no plaintext listener for one to reach. Exceptions ArgumentException The scheme is anything but amqps.

api/Axiam.Sdk.Reactor.ReactorDecision.ht.title: Class ReactorDecision | AXIAM .NET SDK
api/Axiam.Sdk.Reactor.ReactorDecision.ht.summary: Class ReactorDecision Namespace Axiam.Sdk.Reactor Assembly Axiam.Sdk.dll What a handler decided about one event (sdks/CONTRACT.md §22.4). A closed hierarchy of three answers — the abstract base has a private protected constructor, so nothing outside this file can add a fourth. Three of §22.4's rules are encoded here structurally rather than by documentation, because each is a rule an implementation gets wrong by being permissive: allow and patch are mutually exclusive. There is no way to attach a patch to ReactorDecision.Allow — a mutation is a ReactorDecision.Mutate, which serializes decision: "mutate". A patch on an allow is a reply whose author and whose reader disagree about what will happen; the server refuses it rather than resolving it. An empty mutation is malformed. ReactorDecision.Mutate refuses to be constructed with an empty patch, so it cannot be put on the wire and rejected as malformed_mutation at the far end. require_mfa rides on allow. It is a flag on ReactorDecision.Allow, not a fourth decision, and it is valid on login.post_auth only. What is not encoded here is patch filtering. A patch containing a forbidden key is sent unfiltered and rejected by the server (§22.4 rule 1): dropping the bad key would leave the reactor author believing a field was set when it was silently discarded. public abstract class ReactorDecision Inheritance object ReactorDecision Derived ReactorDecision.Allow ReactorDecision.Deny ReactorDecision.Mutate Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Properties Wire The lowercase decision value this answer serializes as. public string Wire { get; } Property Value string Methods AllowRequiringStepUp() Proceed, but only after step-up authentication (login.post_auth only). Step-up is sticky across the chain: once any reactor demands it, no later reactor can clear it. public static ReactorDecision AllowRequiringStepUp() Returns ReactorDecision An ReactorDecision.Allow carrying require_mfa: true. Allowed() Proceed unchanged. public static ReactorDecision Allowed() Returns ReactorDecision An ReactorDecision.Allow with no step-up demand. Denied(string?) Refuse, with an audited reason. public static ReactorDecision Denied(string? reason = null) Parameters reason string Why, for the audit trail; may be null. A deny with no reason still denies — the server substitutes "denied by reactor" when it is absent. Returns ReactorDecision A ReactorDecision.Deny. Mutated(IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>) Proceed with a mutation. public static ReactorDecision Mutated(IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> patch) Parameters patch IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> A non-empty flat map of field name to string value. Returns ReactorDecision A ReactorDecision.Mutate. Exceptions ArgumentException When patch is empty. ArgumentNullException When patch is null.

api/Axiam.Sdk.Reactor.ReactorEvent.html.summary: Class ReactorEvent Namespace Axiam.Sdk.Reactor Assembly Axiam.Sdk.dll One hook firing, delivered to a reactor (sdks/CONTRACT.md §22.3). An instance only ever reaches a handler after ReactorServer has rejected key_version < 2, verified the MAC, checked freshness and checked the nonce, in that order. A runtime that hands an unverified payload to user code has already lost, so this type has no public constructor. The Payload never carries a credential, a token or a signing key: a reactor is told what is being decided, not handed the means to act on it elsewhere. It is not sensitive in the §7 sense and must remain readable — a handler that cannot inspect the event cannot decide anything — but it is tenant business data, so this SDK never logs it, and neither should you at Information level. public sealed class ReactorEvent Inheritance object ReactorEvent Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Fields ReactorPatchKey Payload key under which the server inserts the accumulated patch from earlier reactors in the chain (§22.3). public const string ReactorPatchKey = "_reactor_patch" Field Value string Properties CorrelationId The single-use handle for this dispatch, copied into the reply body by the runtime. Copying it only into the AMQP property produces a reply the server discards. public Guid CorrelationId { get; } Property Value Guid Deadline When this dispatch's window closes. Measured from the moment the delivery arrived plus TimeoutMs, not from IssuedAt: broker latency and clock skew both sit between the two, and a deadline derived from a remote clock would read as already-expired on a reactor whose clock runs slightly fast. public DateTimeOffset Deadline { get; } Property Value DateTimeOffset Event The registry event name, e.g. token.pre_issue. Also the second half of the routing key. public string Event { get; } Property Value string IssuedAt When the server signed this event, already checked to lie within the freshness window. public DateTimeOffset IssuedAt { get; } Property Value DateTimeOffset KeyVersion The §8 envelope version this event was signed under; always at least 2, because a lower one is refused before anything else about the message is considered. public int KeyVersion { get; } Property Value int Nonce The per-message nonce, inside the signed bytes. Not a secret, and safe to log for correlation. public Guid Nonce { get; } Property Value Guid Payload The event-specific body. Never carries a credential, a token or a signing key. public JsonObject Payload { get; } Property Value JsonObject TenantId The tenant this event belongs to; always the tenant this runtime serves. public Guid TenantId { get; } Property Value Guid TimeoutMs How long the server will actually wait for this dispatch, in milliseconds. It is inside the signed body, so it cannot be widened in transit. public int TimeoutMs { get; } Property Value int Methods PriorPatch() The accumulated patch from earlier reactors in the chain (§22.3). When an earlier reactor returned a mutation, the server inserts the merged patch into the payload under ReactorPatchKey before dispatching here, so this reactor decides against the state that will actually be committed. Echoing these keys back inside your own patch is not how a field is preserved — the server merges, with later priority winning a contested key. public IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> PriorPatch() Returns IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> The prior patch, or an empty map when this is the first reactor in the chain (or the only one). api/Axiam.Sdk.Reactor.ReactorEventSpec.h.summary: Class ReactorEventSpec Namespace Axiam.Sdk.Reactor Assembly Axiam.Sdk.dll One hookable event: its name, what a reactor may change, and what happens when the reactor does not answer (sdks/CONTRACT.md §22.5). Mirrors the server's ReactorEventSpec in crates/axiam-core/src/models/reactor.rs, which is the single source of truth. The live copy is served at GET /api/v1/reactors/events; this one is here so a wire contract does not require a network call to be understood. public sealed class ReactorEventSpec Inheritance object ReactorEventSpec Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Properties DefaultFailurePolicy The policy a registration inherits when it names none. public FailurePolicy DefaultFailurePolicy { get; } Property Value FailurePolicy Description One line, as the admin UI shows it. public string Description { get; } Property Value string Interceptable Whether an interceptor may register for this event at all; false means listen-only. public bool Interceptable { get; } Property Value bool Mutable Whether an interceptor's reply may carry a patch. public bool Mutable { get; } Property Value bool MutableFields The complete allow-list: exact field names, or an entry ending in . denoting a namespace prefix. See PatchFieldAllowed(string?). public IReadOnlyList<string> MutableFields { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<string> Name Wire name, and the second half of the routing key (<tenant_id>.<event>). public string Name { get; } Property Value string Methods PatchFieldAllowed(string?) Whether field may appear in a patch for this event. The namespace-prefix rule. An allow-list entry ending in . is a namespace prefix, and it matches a field that starts with the entry and has at least one character after the dot. So ext. admits ext.department and ext.a.b.c, and refuses ext. itself (it names the namespace, not a claim), ext, extra, external_id and evil.ext.department. Everything else follows from that one rule: token.pre_issue cannot reach iss, sub, aud, exp, iat, nbf, jti, scope, scp, azp, act or client_id, because none of them begins with ext.. A hook that can rewrite sub is a hook that can mint a token for anyone, and a correctly signed reply setting sub is refused exactly as a forged one is. This is a read-only predicate. It exists so a reactor author can check a key before writing the handler — it is never used to filter a handler's patch down to the allowed subset, which §22.4 rule 1 forbids. public bool PatchFieldAllowed(string? field) Parameters field string The patch key to test. Returns bool true when the server would accept field here.

This constant list is the same data, restated because a wire contract that requires a network call to be understood is not a contract. §22.7 hot-path exclusion. authz.check, authz.check_batch and token.introspect are not hookable and are absent from Registry and from every constant below. That absence is asserted by a test, not documented by a comment. This SDK also offers no client-side interceptor, middleware hook or callback presenting itself as the reactor equivalent for those operations. api/Axiam.Sdk.Reactor.ReactorHandler.htm.title: Delegate ReactorHandler | AXIAM .NET SDK
api/Axiam.Sdk.Reactor.ReactorHandler.htm.summary: Delegate ReactorHandler Namespace Axiam.Sdk.Reactor Assembly Axiam.Sdk.dll A reactor's decision function: one event in, one of three answers out (sdks/CONTRACT.md §22.10). Invoked only after the runtime has verified the event under §8 v2, so an implementation never sees an unauthenticated payload. Throwing produces no reply. The runtime will not synthesize an allow on your behalf — that would override the operator's fail_closed setting from inside the library. A handler that throws is a reactor that did not answer, and the registration's failure_policy decides what that costs. Answer inside the window. TimeoutMs is how long the server will actually wait. A late reply is discarded and the CPU spent producing it was spent for nothing, so a handler doing expensive work should consult Remaining(DateTimeOffset) and shed load rather than push on. public delegate Task<ReactorDecision> ReactorHandler(ReactorEvent reactorEvent, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Parameters reactorEvent ReactorEvent The verified event. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancelled when the runtime is shutting down. Returns Task<ReactorDecision> The decision to sign and publish; never null.

api/Axiam.Sdk.Reactor.ReactorHandlers.ht.title: Class ReactorHandlers | AXIAM .NET SDK
api/Axiam.Sdk.Reactor.ReactorHandlers.ht.summary: Class ReactorHandlers Namespace Axiam.Sdk.Reactor Assembly Axiam.Sdk.dll Declarative reactor handler binding — CONTRACT.md §22.14. public sealed class ReactorHandlers Inheritance object ReactorHandlers Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks ReactorServer takes one ReactorHandler from an event to one answer, which is the right shape for the wire and the wrong shape for the code. A reactor registered for three events opens with a switch (e.Event), and that switch carries two defects. The first is cheap: a misspelled event name is a valid string, matches no case, and is discovered as an event that never fires. The second is not. It is the default arm, which is almost always written ReactorDecision.Allowed(). That answers on behalf of code that never ran — the defect §22.10 rule 2 forbids the runtime from committing, relocated into user code where the rule does not reach it. An operator who set fail_closed on a registration has it defeated by a default arm in a file they never read. This class is the declarative form, in the spirit of §11's [AxiamAccess]: attribute the methods, collect them, hand the result to ReactorServer. It is pure sugar (§22.14 rule 1): what Handler() returns is exactly the ReactorHandler ReactorServer already accepts. It opens nothing, verifies nothing, signs nothing, and does not filter a patch (§22.10 rule 3). Instances are built once at startup and are not thread-safe to mutate; the delegate Handler() returns snapshots its bindings and is safe for concurrent dispatch. Constructors ReactorHandlers() Creates an empty binding table. Use Bind(string, ReactorHandler) or Of(params object[]). public ReactorHandlers() Methods Bind(string, ReactorHandler) Binds handler to event without an attribute. public ReactorHandlers Bind(string @event, ReactorHandler handler) Parameters event string A §22.5 registry event name. handler ReactorHandler The decision function for that event. Returns ReactorHandlers This instance, for chaining. Remarks The lambda-shaped half of the same thing. Governed by every §22.14 rule identically. Exceptions ArgumentNullException handler is null. ArgumentException event is outside the §22.5 registry — which is how §22.7's hot-path operations are refused, since they are in no registry row — or is already bound. A second binding is a mistake, never a silent overwrite: which of the two runs is not visible from either one. Events() The bound event names, in binding order. public IReadOnlyList<string> Events() Returns IReadOnlyList<string> A read-only list of wire event names. Remarks Pass them to DefaultFailurePolicyFor(IEnumerable<string>) to see what an unreachable reactor costs — the strictest default among them (§22.8) — derived from the code that handles the events rather than from a restatement of the registration. Handler() Composes the bindings into the ReactorHandler ReactorServer accepts. public ReactorHandler Handler() Returns ReactorHandler The composed handler. Exceptions InvalidOperationException Nothing is bound. A reactor that handles nothing would consume its queue and abstain from every event, which looks exactly like an outage. Of(params object[]) Collects every OnReactorEventAttribute-decorated public method on sources. public static ReactorHandlers Of(params object[] sources) Parameters sources object[] Objects whose public methods carry the attribute. Returns ReactorHandlers The collected bindings. Remarks Methods are invoked against the instance they were found on, so a class-based reactor keeps its state and its constructor-injected collaborators. Reflection does not define an order for GetMethods(), so methods are bound in event-name order and Events() is reproducible between runs. ReactorServer is built on this class, and this class is public so an integrator on a transport this SDK does not wrap (a different AMQP client, a test harness, a bridge) can satisfy §22 without reimplementing the one rule that is easy to get wrong. The canonicalization rule. A reactor body is signed with its hmac_signature field present and set to null, in declared field order. That differs from §8's own two message types (AuthzRequest, AuditEventMessage), whose hmac_signature is absent from their canonical bytes — see Hmac, which implements that other rule — and it is the single most likely place for an implementation to produce a MAC that will not verify. Everything else is §8 v2 verbatim: the same HKDF-derived per-tenant subkey, the same HMAC-SHA256 compared in constant time, the same ±300 s freshness window applied in both directions, the same key_version floor of 2. Field order, event (server → reactor): tenant_id, event, correlation_id, payload, timeout_ms, key_version, nonce, issued_at, hmac_signature. Field order, reply (reactor → server): correlation_id, tenant_id, event, decision, reason (omitted when absent), patch (omitted when absent), require_mfa (omitted when false), key_version, nonce, issued_at, hmac_signature. The three conditionally-omitted fields are load-bearing: a reply that serializes "require_mfa": false rather than omitting it produces different canonical bytes and therefore a different MAC. Signing is symmetric in direction. The server signs the event with the tenant subkey; the reactor signs its reply with the same subkey. There is no second key and no asymmetric variant in v1. An unsigned reply is not a weak reply — it is not a reply at all, and the server discards it as though the reactor had never answered. public static class ReactorProtocol Inheritance object ReactorProtocol Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Fields ChainCeilingMs The chain's wall-clock ceiling: past this the remaining reactors are not contacted. public const int ChainCeilingMs = 5000 Field Value int DefaultFreshnessSkew The §8 v2 freshness window applied to issued_at, in both directions. public static readonly TimeSpan DefaultFreshnessSkew Field Value TimeSpan DefaultMaxInFlightPerTenant The server's default per-tenant in-flight interception cap. public const int DefaultMaxInFlightPerTenant = 64 Field Value int DefaultTimeoutMs The timeout_ms a registration gets when it names none (§22.8). public const int DefaultTimeoutMs = 500 Field Value int Exchange The topic exchange every reactor event is published to. public const string Exchange = "axiam.reactor.events" Field Value string KeyVersion The §8 envelope version reactor bodies are signed under. public const int KeyVersion = 2 Field Value int MaxTimeoutMs The largest timeout_ms a registration may name; above this it is refused. public const int MaxTimeoutMs = 5000 Field Value int MinAcceptedKeyVersion The lowest key_version that is even considered. api/Axiam.Sdk.Reactor.ReactorServer.html.summary: Class ReactorServer Namespace Axiam.Sdk.Reactor Assembly Axiam.Sdk.dll The §22 reactor runtime: consume the server-declared queue, verify, decide, sign, reply. Start one with ReactorServeAsync(ReactorServeOptions, CancellationToken). Per delivery it: rejects key_version < 2 — before the signature is even computed; verifies the HMAC over the canonical bytes (§22.2: hmac_signature present and null); checks issued_at against the freshness window, in both directions; checks nonce against a seen-set; then decodes the payload and calls the handler; signs the reply with the same tenant subkey and publishes it to the delivery's reply_to queue, echoing correlation_id both as an AMQP property and — the one the server authenticates — inside the signed body. A runtime that hands an unverified payload to user code has already lost: the handler will act on it, and "we checked afterwards" is not a check. The handler call site here is structurally unreachable until every gate above has passed. Four rules this class holds to It declares no topology. No ExchangeDeclareAsync, no QueueDeclareAsync, no QueueBindAsync, anywhere — asserted by a test against the AMQP client's own recorded invocations. Actors consume; the server declares. It fails closed on its own errors. A handler that throws, or a body it cannot decode, produces no reply — never a synthesized allow. Answering allow on behalf of a handler that crashed would override the operator's fail_closed setting from inside the library. It does not filter a patch. A handler's patch goes on the wire exactly as returned, forbidden keys included. It honours timeout_ms. When the handler returns after the window closed, the reply is abandoned rather than published late — the server has already stopped listening. Interaction with §16, §18 and §19 §16 does not apply to a reply. A correlation is single-use and a late reply is discarded, so re-sending one could only add load to a server that has already moved on. The recovery mechanism for an unanswered dispatch is the registration's failure_policy, on the server, not a retry here. Connection recovery is the RabbitMQ client's, left on exactly as AxiamAmqpConsumer leaves it. §18: DisposeAsync() is idempotent, cancels the consumer so no new delivery starts, drains what is in flight up to the configured grace period, and does not close the caller's channel or connection. §19: one RequestStart/RequestEnd pair per dispatched event, with the event name as the path template — a closed set of five values, so it cannot become a cardinality bomb. public sealed class ReactorServer : IAsyncDisposable Inheritance object ReactorServer Implements IAsyncDisposable Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Fields DefaultShutdownGrace The drain grace period DisposeAsync() uses when none was configured. public static readonly TimeSpan DefaultShutdownGrace Field Value TimeSpan TelemetryMethod The §19 "method" label for an AMQP dispatch. public const string TelemetryMethod = "AMQP" Field Value string TelemetryOperation The §19 operation name every reactor telemetry event carries. public const string TelemetryOperation = "ReactorServeAsync" Field Value string Properties InFlight How many events are being handled right now; drains to zero during shutdown. public int InFlight { get; } Property Value int IsClosed Whether DisposeAsync() has run. public bool IsClosed { get; } Property Value bool Queue The server-declared queue this runtime consumes. public string Queue { get; } Property Value string Methods DisposeAsync() Stops serving, deterministically (§18). Cancels the consumer first so no new delivery can start, then waits for in-flight handlers up to the configured grace period. Idempotent. It does not close the channel or the connection — the caller owns those, exactly as AxiamAmqpConsumer leaves them. public ValueTask DisposeAsync() Returns ValueTask A task that completes once the drain finishes or the grace period elapses. Write it idempotently. A redelivery after a broker hiccup is normal. A listener that double-counts is a listener that was assuming exactly-once delivery it was never promised.

api/Axiam.Sdk.Webauthn.WebauthnFailure.h.summary: Enum WebauthnFailure Namespace Axiam.Sdk.Webauthn Assembly Axiam.Sdk.dll A ceremony failure a caller can say something useful about (CONTRACT.md §24.6b rule 5). public enum WebauthnFailure Extension Methods WebauthnFailures.Message(WebauthnFailure) Fields AlreadyRegistered = 1 The authenticator already holds a credential for this account and refused to silently mint a second — the exclusion list working, not a failure. The only classification whose remedy is "use a different device". Cancelled = 0 Covers both an explicit refusal and a silent timeout. The WebAuthn spec deliberately refuses to distinguish them, because telling a website which one happened leaks whether an authenticator was present. It must not be recovered by timing the call. Timeout = 2 An explicitly aborted ceremony. Unknown = 4 Everything else. Unsupported = 3 This device or browser cannot run the ceremony. Remarks This SDK ships no linked-API helper — a server or CLI runtime has no authenticator and §24.6b rule 2 forbids emulating one — but the classification is still required of it: a Blazor or MAUI front end relaying a DOMException name has the same five outcomes and the same reason to want one vocabulary for them.

Mirrors the server's signer (crates/axiam-api-rest/src/webhook.rs's compute_signature_v2): the MAC covers the ASCII string <t>.<raw_body>, keyed with the webhook secret's raw UTF-8 bytes. public static class AxiamWebhooks Inheritance object AxiamWebhooks Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Fields DefaultTolerance The default freshness window (CONTRACT.md §13.2): a signature whose t= is more than this far in the past OR the future (relative to timeProvider's clock — see Verify(Sensitive<string>, string, ReadOnlySpan<byte>, TimeSpan?, TimeProvider?)) is rejected. public static readonly TimeSpan DefaultTolerance Field Value TimeSpan Methods Verify(Sensitive<string>, string, ReadOnlySpan<byte>, TimeSpan?, TimeProvider?) Verifies a webhook delivery's X-Axiam-Signature header against body and returns the parsed WebhookEvent on success. public static WebhookEvent Verify(Sensitive<string> secret, string signatureHeader, ReadOnlySpan<byte> body, TimeSpan? tolerance = null, TimeProvider? timeProvider = null) Parameters secret Sensitive<string> The webhook's plaintext signing secret (CONTRACT.md §7 Sensitive<T>). Its raw UTF-8 bytes are the HMAC key. Wrap a bare string with Wrap(T). signatureHeader string The raw, unparsed X-Axiam-Signature header value — t=<unix_seconds>,v1=<hex>, optionally with multiple v1 entries during secret rotation. body ReadOnlySpan<byte> The exact raw bytes received off the wire, before any JSON parsing. Re-serializing a parsed body (different key order/whitespace) changes these bytes and breaks the MAC — callers MUST buffer and pass the untouched request body. In ASP.NET Core this means enabling HttpRequest.EnableBuffering() (or reading the body stream directly) before any model binder has had a chance to parse and re-serialize it. tolerance TimeSpan? The freshness window; null or a non-positive value falls back to DefaultTolerance (300 seconds). Rejects a t= more than this far in the past OR the future — a two-sided check, so a future-dated timestamp is rejected just like a stale one (clock-skew abuse). timeProvider TimeProvider Test/injection seam for "now"; defaults to System. Pass a fake TimeProvider to deterministically exercise the freshness check. Returns WebhookEvent The verified, parsed WebhookEvent. Exceptions WebhookVerificationException The header is malformed (no v1, more than one t, non-numeric t, or empty), no supplied v1 matches the recomputed MAC, or t falls outside the freshness tolerance. The exception message is always a fixed, generic reason string — never the expected signature or the secret (CONTRACT.md §13.3 rule 6).

Both fields ship with byte-identical content until AXIAM 2.0, where this one is removed; new code MUST read reason and MUST NOT depend on this field surviving. Either, both or neither member may be set; a claim with NEITHER set names a confirmation method this server version does not implement. The consumer rule is the same one SDK contract §10.1 rule 9 makes normative, and it is the whole reason this message exists: a confirmation the consumer cannot check MUST be refused, never read as "unconstrained". index.html.summary: AXIAM .NET SDK API reference for the AXIAM .NET packages: Axiam.Sdk — the client: cookie-session authentication (LoginAsync, VerifyMfaAsync, RefreshAsync, LogoutAsync), authorization (CheckAccessAsync, BatchCheckAsync), the gRPC authorization client, the OIDC/SSO relying-party helpers (OidcDiscoverAsync, OidcBegin, OidcExchangeAsync, OidcRefreshAsync, LoginClientCredentialsAsync, IntrospectAsync, RevokeAsync, SsoStartAsync, SsoCompleteAsync), and the AMQP consumer with HMAC verification and replay protection. Axiam.Sdk.AspNetCore — the resource-server middleware for ASP.NET Core: verifies the AXIAM JWT locally against a cached JWKS, enforces the cross-tenant claim check, applies the CSRF double-submit check to cookie-authenticated state-changing requests, and wires the "Login with AXIAM" OIDC login/callback endpoints (MapAxiamOidcLogin). See the AXIAM SDK contract for the behaviour every AXIAM SDK guarantees.
